articles.title_zh: Opinion | Europe still has no clear goal on China
articles.content_orig:
A Europe that gives China its price list and the US its autonomy can only buy small concessions, leaving its ‘kill switch’ unused
This month alone, Europe has threatened China with a trade “kill switch”, rebuked it in parliament, sent its trade commissioner on a much-trumpeted trip to Beijing and announced three new economic security instruments.
The sequence exposed a European Union that has no clear goal on China, no hierarchy of priorities and has reached no agreement on what it wants from Beijing or on what it would pay to get it.

articles.title_zh: Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled. See affected products
articles.content_orig:
Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste were recalled by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Oct. 19, including some popular children's brands.
The recall was initiated voluntarily by Pritam International Private Limited on Sept. 10, according to a FDA report . The agency has classified the recall as Class II on Oct. 19.
The recall includes multiple varieties of Brush Buddies kids toothpaste that are distributed nationwide, including products targeted to kids such as character-themed and ice-cream flavored toothpastes.
The recall also included two types of Evo products marketed for teeth whitening and sensitivity, and two Aru products marketed for gum health and cavity protection.
According to the FDA, a Class II recall is issued when the use of a product "may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote."
The FDA did not give a reason for the toothpaste recall. USA TODAY contacted the agency, which did not immediately respond to a request for more information.
The FDA's enforcement report lists several varieties of Brush Buddies children's toothpaste, including Hot Wheels-themed and My Little Pony-themed flavors, in addition to chocolate ice cream flavored, cookies 'n cream flavored and mint chocolate chip flavored flavors.

articles.title_orig: Who blinked first? Fragile EU-China trade peace sparks new war of words
articles.title_zh: Who blinked first? Fragile EU-China trade peace sparks new war of words
articles.content_orig:
As European officials flag more trade restrictions, Beijing bristles at the idea it can be pushed into yielding to Brussels’ demands
In Brussels and Berlin, officials are emboldened by what they consider proof that collective EU pressure can force Chinese concessions. Rather than resting on their laurels, they are cooking up a fresh batch of trade restrictions.
Beijing, on the other hand, has bristled at the idea that it can be strong-armed into yielding to Europe’s demands, even more so the suggestion that further concessions may be coming. State media has carried numerous warnings against European hubris.
It has resulted in an awkward, terse trade peace: an agreement that was supposed to defuse a trade war has led to both sides, rhetorically at least, hardening their positions. With verbal volleys flying back and forth, doubts are already surfacing over whether this delicate ceasefire can hold until the next round of negotiations in January.

articles.title_zh: American Express brings Airbnb bookings and rewards to Amex Travel platform
articles.content_orig:
American Express is bringing Airbnb into its travel rewards platform.
The companies on Thursday announced a new partnership to bring more than 1 million Airbnb listings to Amex's travel portal and allow cardholders to earn rewards when booking the stays. It does not currently allow members to redeem points to pay for Airbnb bookings.
The launch adds Airbnb rentals to Amex's hotel portfolio, which includes more than 3,400 properties across its Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection programs.
Amex members with either the consumer or business Platinum card can also now apply their $600 annual lodging credit — previously called the hotel credit — to Airbnb's higher-end Luxe stays and take advantage of a new $250 statement credit on eligible Airbnb Experiences after making a Luxe booking.
"We're excited to bring more choice and flexibility to American Express Card Members with this exclusive partnership. Both of our companies exist to help people travel more and better, and this partnership helps people see more of the world by making travel more rewarding," said Juan David Borrero, head of partnerships at Airbnb, in a news release.
Membership points vary by card:
The changes come as competition among premium credit cards continues to ramp up.
Last year, American Express raised the annual fee on its premium Platinum card to $895. In turn, it's been investing in cardholder perks such as new lounges in airports and at big-ticket events and experiences as a way to attract more high-paying customers.
Earlier this month, it announced an expansion of its Centurion Lounges , with renovations coming to four existing lounges and new ones planned for Newark Liberty International Airport and London Heathrow Airport. The Newark lounge will be the largest in its network.
The partnership also comes as Americans continue to opt for travel and luxury experiences, even as prices for airfare, gas and hotels rise. Despite higher costs, more than half of Americans reported making no changes to their travel plans this summer , a recent study by travel insurance company Squaremouth found.

articles.title_orig: Horrifying video shows Mexican teen falling to her death from carnival ride
articles.title_zh: Horrifying video shows Mexican teen falling to her death from carnival ride
articles.content_orig:
A Mexican teenager died after falling from a carnival ride, with horrific video showing her flying out of her seat as the ride reached full speed.
Gabriela Rodriguez Tezoco, 18, died on Tuesday night following the accident at a festival in Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, local outlet Expreso reported .
Cell phone footage taken by another rider shows Tezoco plummeting to the ground from “The Pendulum,” a spinning ride at the Cabo San Lucas Traditional Festivals.
Other riders could be heard screaming as the teenager fell off while the ride kept spinning at high speed.
Emergency services rushed to treat Tezoco, who was taken to a nearby hospital, where she sadly died from her injuries early Wednesday morning.
“It is with deep sorrow that we report that the young woman who was injured in the incident that occurred in the amusement park area of ​​the Cabo San Lucas Traditional Festivals, and who was immediately transferred to receive medical attention, lost her life despite the efforts of the health personnel,” the Los Cabos City Council wrote on social media.
“The Pendulum” ride was closed in the wake of the incident while safety tests are carried out on it and the other attractions at the fair, Los Cabos mayor Christian Agundez told local reporters.
“Today, with the same spirit with which we come together to celebrate, we must come together to support Gabriela’s family. It could have been any one of us. You are not alone,” Agundez said during an appearance at a concert which was part of the festival.
An investigation has been opened both into the circumstances and to determine potential liability, the Baja California Sur State Attorney General’s Office reported on Wednesday.
So far, no arrests have been made, and no one responsible for the ride’s operation has been publicly identified.
Tezoco had just graduated this summer from the Baja California Sur College of Baccalaureate Studies.
“May your smile remain alive in our memory and may your memory always be a light that guides us,” the school said in a tribute.

articles.title_orig: Global Rush to Fix Security Flaw Uncovered by A.I. Leaves Sites Offline
articles.title_zh: Global Rush to Fix Security Flaw Uncovered by A.I. Leaves Sites Offline
articles.content_orig:
Government and company websites around the world briefly went dark and suspended some services, as operators scrambled to patch their systems after artificial intelligence helped find critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language.
Nearly three dozen UK government services are unavailable and four are “partially unavailable” while security upgrades take place, UK government minister Elizabeth Lloyd told the House of Lords Thursday. “No large public-facing critical services are being affected by the exercise but some limited services may temporarily be offline while security work is carried out,” a UK government spokesperson told reporters.
The US National Security Agenc y and Europe’s cybersecurity agency have advised companies to take immediate action to address two critical flaws in PHP, a programming language that powers 70% of all websites in the world, including WordPress and Drupal, an open-source content management system.
The PHP Foundation, the organization behind the coding language, has released a patch for the bugs, which have been hidden in their software for years, and is urging website operators to update their systems immediately.
Popular Irish news website The Journal was temporarily offline Thursday morning while it bolstered its “defences,” it said in a notice. The Journal is Ireland’s second most-used online news source, behind only RTÉ, the national broadcaster, according to the Reuters Institute.
The flaws in PHP – which originally stood for Personal Home Page – were uncovered by teams at OpenAI , Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz, and another cybersecurity company, Calif . The bugs, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to hack into websites and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords.
“With PHP behind such a vast share of the web, the exposure could reach almost everywhere people spend money online,” said Nigel Green, the CEO of deVere Group, a financial advisory firm.
“Booking platforms, marketplaces, subscription services, ticketing sites, delivery apps and utility portals could all be holding card details on systems built with the same kind of code,” he added.
Even world leaders urged organizations to take action. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that his cabinet was “closely monitoring the situation surrounding the vulnerabilities in PHP.”
Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said companies should consider suspending services if necessary in order to reduce their exposure. “Please check if your publicly available websites use PHP, and prepare to apply the fix patch that will be released tonight… as soon as possible,” she posted on X Wednesday.
Japanese airline ANA, railway operator JR West and the country’s largest bank, MUFG, were among companies that reported some webpages and services temporarily suspended.
In Europe, government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands, including the Dutch cyber security agency, were temporarily taken offline while security fixes were implemented.
The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia, told CNN Thursday that it was “in the process of addressing security vulnerabilities in PHP,” and that a number of its systems had been taken down as a “precautionary measure.”
AI played a crucial role in finding and fixing vulnerabilities “that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade,” according to Wiz, which said the episode marks an “AI inflection point.”
“What AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post Wednesday in which they described PHP as a “backbone of the web.”
“With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work,” they added.
The bugs were discovered in late August but were disclosed to the public only on Wednesday, after PHP had come up with a fix.
The flaws could allow attackers to remotely execute code, disrupt services and expose customer data, according to web infrastructure provider Cloudflare, which has been working with the PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI and Wiz to address the issue.
Researchers at Wiz used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol during the research process.
Wiz researchers say the issue is on par with the Heartbleed bug from 2014, which impacted an encryption technology estimated to be used by two-thirds of the Web. Heartbleed allowed cybercriminals to access data that should have been protected.
Like Heartbleed, the researchers at Wiz say PHP2Shell could similarly serve as a turning point in cybersecurity. While the vulnerabilities existed for years, AI made it practical to deploy them.
“The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” the researchers said.
“Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.”
– CNN’s John Liu, Anna Cooban, Amy Croffey and James Frater contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Late detection in Nigeria raises alarm as Ebola spreads across Africa
articles.title_zh: Late detection in Nigeria raises alarm as Ebola spreads across Africa
articles.content_orig:
Nigerian health officials say test results have confirmed the country’s first case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which is behind a major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), marking the disease’s first spread to West Africa in the current outbreak.
The case involves a woman who travelled from Uganda to the capital, Abuja, on October 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.
She was tested for Ebola on October 19 after health officials learned she had recently travelled to Uganda, one of the countries affected by the current outbreak. Officials confirmed the positive result on Tuesday.
“We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, director of the public health laboratory service at the NCDC, said on Wednesday.
The World Health Organization (WHO) also confirmed the strain, for which there is neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.
An unnamed official told the AFP news agency that the woman is a diplomat whose condition has deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”.
Ayoade Alakija, a Nigerian physician who co-chairs a G7 committee for investment in global health, said that it had taken 12 days since the woman fell sick for her to be tested for Ebola, potentially exposing many other people to the infection.
Nigerian authorities have identified 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers. They include the patient’s husband, a Swiss national, who lives with her in Abuja.
Officials are also tracing passengers who travelled with her from Uganda to Nigeria but do not believe she was symptomatic during the flight.
Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told public broadcaster NTA that the woman was in isolation and receiving treatment.
In 2014, the first Nigerian case, detected in Lagos, raised fears the virus would spread rapidly, but it was brought under control within three months, resulting in 20 infections and eight deaths.
That epidemic killed more than 11,000 people across West Africa between late 2013 and 2016.
The WHO says Nigeria is the fifth country to detect the virus in the outbreak, which this past week widened across the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6.
Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Director-General Jean Kaseya said on X on Wednesday that the outbreak was “no longer one country’s fight”, and that he would hold a meeting of Africa’s health ministers next week to strengthen the cross-border response and review hospital capacity.
The DRC is the epicentre of the outbreak, its deadliest on record.
There have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and more than 4,000 deaths there since mid-May.

articles.title_orig: German youth plan France-style mass protests
articles.title_zh: German youth plan France-style mass protests
articles.content_orig:
"Gen Z regelt" — or Gen Z's Got It — a youth initiative, has called for mass protests in 21 cities across Germany on Saturday, October 31; including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Munich.
Thousands are expected to participate in demonstrations protesting "broken schools and austerity," as well as the cost of living, social injustice, military conscription and climate change.
French protests that exploded in violence and rampant destruction of private and public property this weekend also grew out of student frustration over the national school system and soon included numerous unions , groups and individuals voicing anger over a number of issues.
Gen Z regelt's website clearly states that the initiative is "against all violence," whether directed at people or property.
Police say they are "vigilant and relaxed," adding that they intend to protect people's right to congregate and express their opinions.
Still, images of massive damage and public violence from France , Italy and Spain have raised concerns among domestic policymakers and police, who have warned against allowing the protests to be hijacked by left-wing extremists.
Andreas Roßkopf, head of the German Federal Police's GdP union, made clear that officers would deal harshly with riots and rioters, telling the Rheinische Post newspaper on Wednesday, "state, but also federal police, will offer a firm and decisive response" to any trouble.
Roßkopf also warned that radicals and extremists could insert themselves among demonstrators in order to "attack police" or "simply be destructive."

articles.title_orig: Far-left leader Melenchon in firing line as France blame-game heats up
articles.title_zh: Far-left leader Melenchon in firing line as France blame-game heats up
articles.content_orig:
Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the riots’ chief instigator and leader of the far-left La France Insoumise (LFI), is currently ranked second in most presidential polls. Marine Le Pen remains the favourite despite her continuing legal problems.
But the polls do not reveal Mélenchon’s strategy, his organisation, his coherence or his ruthlessness. It has become fashionable to dismiss his chances. He is too radical, they say, too inflammatory. As if that has not benefited other modern underdogs.
Born in Tangier in 1951, the former socialist schoolteacher became a senator at 35 and briefly served as a minister under the former PM Lionel Jospin. Mélenchon has spent the past 18 years building a party in his own image. This is his fourth presidential run, and there has been steady progress: in 2022 he came within a point and a half of the second round.
Mélenchon is quite obviously brilliant. Contrary to most other French politicians, who have the literacy of dried oysters, he is well-read and can speak well. He can cite Victor Hugo, whose parliamentary speeches he reveres as much as Les Misérables , as well as Robespierre and Michelet’s history of the Revolution. He is what the French call a tribun , a tribune, an orator, who regularly summons countless minions. His rally in June in Saint-Denis united tens of thousands of people.
Mélenchon has built a formidable political machine. It is hierarchical and motivated, possibly more so than any other party’s. In France, the trained ear can spot when his circle has held one of its internal strategy meetings: rumours start spreading, all using the same turns of phrase.
His team has adapted old-school Red methods to the modern world. Woe betide the victim of their online legions, who will barrage you with threats and insults for days. I was turned into a target after I allegedly argued for the expulsion of Algerian diplomats and the burning of their Paris embassy, following the incarceration of the writer Boualem Sansal.
Mélenchon’s lieutenants owe him every-thing and are quite ready to die for him. They are his Red Guard. First among equals is Manuel Bompard – doctor of applied mathematics, campaign director in 2017 and 2022, elected to his boss’s old seat in Marseille. He is the brains. Next comes Mathilde Panot. An international relations graduate from Sciences Po university, and now president of the parliamentary group, she is the enforcer, a woman who could credibly pass as a territorial and domineering 14th-century tavern keeper. Then there is Sophia Chik-irou, communications director and almost certainly in a relationship with Mélenchon (the leader of the Communist party has called LFI a sect under the spell of a couple).
Add to that the lower rungs, peopled with creatures of marsupial intelligence: National Assembly member Sébastien Delogu, the barely literate Marseille taxi driver whose only qualification is his cab licence; European Parliament member Rima Hassan, born in a Syrian refugee camp and turned ambassador to Gaza, who went on trial this week for glorifying terrorism; Raphaël Arnault, also in the National Assembly, who sits on a state security watchlist and co-founded the Jeune Garde. This is the outfit whose militants are under investigation for the death of 23-year-old Quentin Deranque, bludgeoned to oblivion in a Lyon street in February. Two of those charged with involvement were Arnault’s own parliamentary assistants.
Mélenchon has purged the party of any-one who isn’t deathly loyal. A number of old-timers, some of whom co-founded LFI with him, were ruthlessly cast out and blacklisted after an attempted modern leftist version of a marshals’ mutiny just before the snap election of 2024. The rebels told Mélenchon he was too tainted to be the party’s presidential nominee and should step aside. Five days later, most had official LFI candidates running against them, and their names were no longer mentioned by many former colleagues.
The rebels included my friend Alexis Corbière, an old companion of Mélenchon’s, who, despite the purge, managed to hold on to his seat in the Assembly. His experience featured prominently in a book on the brutality of LFI’s Stalinist tactics, entitled La Meute (‘The Pack’), which enjoyed considerable commercial success.
These lovely characters built LFI’s think-tank: the Institut la Boétie, founded in October 2019 by Bernard Pignerol, a councillor of state and an old friend of the boss. (Étienne de La Boétie wrote Discourse on Voluntary Servitude , a 16th-century essay explaining why whole peoples consent to serve one man…) It’s a facility with impressive political output – a stream of graduates from ten-weekend courses – financed by a million-euro grant from the party and tax-deductible donations which have been referred to the Treasury for scrutiny.
Woe betide the victim of their online legions, who will barrage you with threats and insults for days
Out of the Institut’s orbit come blue-haired ideologues and, far more dangerous, the sleeper agents: some 80 senior civil servants calling themselves the Phrygians, formed in May this year. They meet each month, co-ordinate by Telegram, and embed themselves at the finance ministry, the foreign ministry, the Banque de France and the European Commission. Their handler is the beautiful Clémence Guetté, who co-chairs the Institut with Mélenchon and runs the programme.
No other political family or faction in modern France is as well organised as LFI. This is one hell of a tight ship. I would willingly grant that their presidential prospects are poor for this cycle. But I would not be so bold as to dismiss their chances entirely.
LFI has something no other party seems able to hold on to: a disciplined strategy for attaining and keeping power. They have bet everything on Islam and its representatives, abandoning the workers of old in favour of immigrants and their descendants.
Sixty-nine per cent of French Muslims voted for Mélenchon in the first round of 2022. It is a bloc more cohesive than any other group voting for anyone, anywhere (he scored 88 per cent in some areas). If demographic curves are to be believed – which they are – this is bound to be a winning strategy, if not next year, then soon.
But Mélenchon would also be wise not to trust in his own invincibility. He may yet be consumed by his new friends, who have proven, on more than one occasion, perfectly willing to devour their own.

Meta stockholders are set to receive free shares if Mark Zuckerberg absolutely crushes it as CEO.
The social-media giant revealed in a Wednesday filing that if its upcoming Class C shares double from a baseline price of $580.60 to just over $1,161, and their compound annualized return since September 10 has been at least 10%, shareholders will receive a dividend: a Class C share for every Meta share they own.
If Meta stock — specifically its 30-day volume-weighted average price — doubles again to around $2,322, and has risen by at least 10% on average per year, shareholders will receive the same dividend again, and so on.
Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and the AI agent Muse , acknowledged how difficult it will be to unlock those dividends, describing the stock price targets as "extraordinary" in its filing.
Its stock has already surged more than sevenfold from its November 2022 low, giving Meta a nearly $1.8 trillion market capitalization that ranks it among the 10 most valuable companies in the world.
The additional dividends would be paid on top of the initial dividend declared by Meta's board on Wednesday, which will see Class A and Class B shareholders receive Class C shares on a 1:1 basis, likely in late January.
Meta is rejigging its share structure in response to Zuckerberg's concerns about California's so-called billionaire tax: a one-off, 5% wealth tax on the roughly 250 billionaires living in the state.
Zuckerberg, who ranked fifth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index with a $247 billion net worth at Wednesday's close, will be able to sell the Class C shares to access the liquidity needed to pay the tax, avoiding a sale of his existing shares that would erode his voting power .
Meta's board took action after Zuckerberg said he was considering moving out of California because of the potential tax, and cautioned that the steps involved in relocating, such as listing his home for sale, could spark questions from employees about the company's management, the filing says.

Top European diplomats will hold talks in Istanbul Friday with their counterparts from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt during a meeting initiated by Ankara, a Turkish foreign ministry source told the AFP news agency on Thursday.
Foreign ministers from the so-called E3 group – Britain, France and Germany – will meet counterparts from the newly created R4 group to discuss the Palestinian issue, developments in Yemen and the Strait of Hormuz and ways to end the Russia-Ukraine war, the source said.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will host the meeting, the first to bring together the two groups.
"The seven countries will come together for the first time in the R4+E3 format, at Turkey's initiative," the source said, indicating they would explore "opportunities for cooperation and coordination that could be put into practice ... in the coming period."
In chairing the meeting, Fidan was expected to focus on the international community "increasing pressure on Israel" in response to its settlement expansion and its "encouragement of settler terrorism," the source AFP.
Fidan will also underline support for Saudi Arabia's security in the face of attacks by Yemen's Houthis, and stress the need for permanent freedom of navigation in the Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Straits.
Saudi Arabia's state-owned Saudi Aramco, the world's biggest oil company, told staff to evacuate the company's headquarters in the eastern city of Dhahran and to work remotely, the Reuters news agency reported Thursday, citing six sources with knowledge of the matter.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have hit the kingdom repeatedly with missile and drone attacks in recent weeks.
Last week a missile struck an Aramco building in Dhahran, which is on Saudi Arabia's Persian Gulf coast. The strike caused a "limited fire" at Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex, the kingdom's energy ministry said at the time.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen's escalating civil war said Thursday that it had intercepted another drone over the Saudi capital Riyadh.
Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki confirmed the interception in a social media post, without offering further details.
Saudi Arabia has been pummeled by Houthi strikes in recent weeks. Experts say geography, missile interceptor shortages and evolving Houthi tactics are helping the Iranian proxy menace the kingdom, and global energy supplies .
World shares and U.S. futures retreated Thursday as oil prices jumped more than 2% following a report by Iran's state television that seven oil tankers were hit by its military or sea mines and damaged near the Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf.
If the claim by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is verified, it would be the largest number of vessels damaged in the Gulf in a single day since the start of the Iran war on Feb. 28.
Brent crude, the international standard, gained 3.2% to hit $112.27 per barrel Thursday. It has been bouncing around $110 in recent days amid uncertainty about when the war with Iran might ease to allow the global energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to return to normal.
U.S. benchmark crude rose 2.8% to $99.80 per barrel.
In early European trading, Germany's DAX shed 1.1% to 25,367.96, while the CAC 40 in Paris declined 1.3% to 7,816.67. Britain's FTSE 100 was down 0.7% at 10,678.67.
The future for the S&P 500 lost 1% and that for the Dow Jones Industrial Average was 0.7% lower.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Thursday that it had struck four vessels transferring oil ship-to-ship in the Persian Gulf after they used a route through the Strait of Hormuz that Iran rejects. Ship-to-ship cargo transfers have become more common as tankers and other commercial vessels try to avoid Iranian detection and strikes in the strategic waterway.
In a statement, the IRGC Navy said it "monitored and pursued four violating vessels that had previously passed through an illegal route," referring to shipping lanes in the strait that the Trump administration has encouraged vessels to use to avoid Iranian fees and controls. Tehran considers those southern routes, close to Oman's coast, unauthorized and has targeted vessels trying to use them for months.
"They discovered the vessels transferring oil cargoes from ship to ship in the north-central part of the Persian Gulf," the bulletin read. "All four ships were hit simultaneously and are burning."
The IRGC said three other ships attempting to use routes not recognized by Iran "suffered accidents and caught fire after striking mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, and were brought to a halt."
The IRGC said the U.S. "encouraging vessels to pass through an illegally mined passage has led to an increasing number of maritime incidents day by day."
"If this course continues," the group warned, "the confrontation will extend to the bases of the aggressors in the region."
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said Thursday that the latest attack on the kingdom's airports, a strike on the eastern city of Dammam's King Fahd International Airport, had risen to two.
"The number of deaths resulting from the attack has risen to two, after confirming an additional death. The deceased were a Saudi citizen and a resident of Indian nationality," the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement shared on social media.
It said eight others, "a Saudi citizen, two residents each of Indian, Yemeni, and Bangladeshi nationalities, and a resident of Nepalese nationality," were injured in the attack.
The statement did not assign blame for the attack, but Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen have attacked Saudi airports and other infrastructure for weeks in retaliation for the Saudi government's backing of Yemeni state forces in the neighboring nation's decade-long civil war.
GACA said in its statement that it was continuing work in conjunction with other security authorities "to assess the damages, and to take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and employees, and to maintain the security and safety of the civil aviation system in the Kingdom."
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks have inflicted severe losses on the kingdom and prompted the U.S. to quietly reduce its military footprint in the region as missiles hit energy infrastructure and civilian airports, killing more than 20 people.
Saudi Arabia, despite its size, wealth and a substantial military, has appeared to be on the back foot as it faces the Yemeni rebels.
Saudi Arabia spent $83 billion on defense last year, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute — far more than any other country in the Middle East , including Israel.
So, why has the kingdom struggled to stop the Houthi barrage? Read our full story here .
An attack targeting the King Fahd International Airport in the eastern Saudi Arabian city of Dammam killed one person and injured eight others Wednesday evening, the kingdom's civil aviation authority said.
The authority said in a statement that injuries from the attack ranged from "minor to serious" and that material damage to the airport was also being assessed.
It did not describe what type of attack occurred, but the kingdom's airports have been targeted repeatedly by projectiles in recent days by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants.
A U.S. official and a senior U.S. military official told CBS News on Wednesday the military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing regional threats from the Houthis and direct threats from Iran.
NBC News was first to report on the drawdowns.
Asked about the reports, U.S. Central Command spokesperson Capt. Tim Hawkins told CBS News: "We regularly move U.S. service members and assets to optimize mission readiness. We do not discuss related movements for operational security reasons. U.S. forces remain vigilant and ready to protect American personnel and interests across the region."

STRASBOURG — The International Criminal Court has won this year's Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought, awarded by the European Parliament, according to two people with knowledge of the decision.
The €50,000 prize honors defenders of human rights and freedom of thought, with past winners including Nelson Mandela, Alexei Navalny, Belarusian journalists, and the people of Ukraine.
The Socialists and Democrats group nominated the ICC following U.S. President Donald Trump's sanctions on the court, announced on Oct. 9.
"We stand by the ICC and its officials, and we are committed to safeguarding its work. We must guarantee that the ICC is able to operate independently, free from pressure or external interference," said S&D vice-chair Yannis Maniatis in early October. "It is a people-based organization, not a political one. If the aggressors become the victims, and if we stand by helplessly as international justice erodes, we risk allowing those who believe themselves above the law to prevail."
The prize is named in honor of Andrei Sakharov, a Soviet physicist and political dissident. Shortlisted candidates are traditionally invited to the Parliament’s award ceremony, which takes place during the December plenary session in Strasbourg.

articles.title_zh: Toyota recalls over 105,000 vehicles. See the affected model
articles.content_orig:
Toyota has issued a rather strange recall for the 2024-2027 Land Cruiser . It also seems rather comprehensive; the recall population numbers 105,794, which is nearabout the total number of Land Cruisers sold in the U.S. so far for the current J250 generation.
The issue stems from a retaining clip that connects fuel tubes from the gas tank to the engine. Specifically, there’s a resin fuel tube on the tank that connects to a main metal fuel tube, the latter of which delivers gas to the engine. Toyota says that if the retaining clip on the connector between the two is lifted, there’s a possibility of a fuel leak—and of course, a fuel leak means an increased chance of fire.
Toyota conducted a years-long investigation into this issue, starting all the way back in July 2024. You can read the full timeline of events here , but we’ll summarize the six-page document for you.
Toyota became aware of the issue when field reports noted the retainer clip holding the fuel tubes together was lifted or missing. How this happened was vigorously investigated, but Toyota found no issues in the part or its manufacturing processes. One theory suggested in the report is that some recovered connectors showed evidence of markings that could’ve been caused by someone disconnecting the tubes after manufacturing. Additionally, other markings seen on certain clips were consistent with prior supplier testing.
When it comes to the fire risk, Toyota says it evaluated the temperatures of nearby components, finding all of them below the ignition temperature of fuel.
The most recent testing from Toyota this year attempted to identify how the retainer clip at this connection could become lifted. None of the tests provided the information Toyota was looking for; that said, among 400 field vehicles where no connector disconnects had been alleged / leaks reported, Toyota identified one with a lifted retainer clip. Despite the clip being lifted, that one vehicle was not leaking fuel.
Toyota ultimately decided to conduct this recall based on its fuel leak volume evaluation, and the number of field cases it observed of the clip being lifted. As of this recall, Toyota is aware of 23 field reports and 64 warranty claims that relate to the issue. With the cause and circumstances around how the issue manifests, Toyota is unsure what percentage of vehicles might contain this defect.
The fix is relatively simple. Dealers will inspect the connection and install a supplemental clamp. If necessary, they’ll replace the resin fuel tube, too. Notifications to owners are expected to occur by December 13 this year, and per federal law , all recall work will be completed free of charge.

Apple's newly unveiled foldable iPhone Duo sparks significant consumer interest despite a hefty $1,999 starting price tag. On 'Varney & Co.', Taylor Riggs explains the premium device's unique dual-screen capability and ultra-thin design. Host Stuart Varney admits he plans to purchase the high-end smartphone, which can cost up to $3,000 for the two-terabyte storage model.
Your iPhone probably holds more personal information than your wallet. Think about the passwords you've saved, the photos you never intended to share and the private notes you keep handy. Now, security researchers have uncovered a more aggressive version of spyware designed to get its hands on that information.
The threat is called P7 DarkSword, and researchers at mobile security company iVerify discovered it while investigating an infected iPhone. According to their Oct. 8, 2026, report, the spyware can collect sensitive information and communicate with attackers who can issue additional commands remotely.
That sounds alarming, and it should get your attention. However, the research does not establish that every iPhone is vulnerable. Here's what researchers discovered and how you can better protect your device.
YOUR PHONE SAYS IT'S UPDATED. CHECK OTHER SETTINGS, TOO
Researchers discovered a stealthier version of DarkSword spyware that can secretly collect personal information and receive commands from attackers. (iStock)

You'll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.
P7 DarkSword is a newly identified variant of DarkSword, an existing iPhone spyware family. Researchers at iVerify discovered it while investigating a suspicious infection in August 2026. Their security system had flagged unusual activity on a customer's device. After examining the phone with the customer's permission, the team discovered that the spyware behaved differently from versions they had previously encountered.
The researchers also searched for related malicious code using the Validin threat intelligence platform. Eventually, they identified another version of the spyware hosted on suspicious infrastructure. Their analysis revealed that the attackers had modified the code to make it more capable and harder to investigate. The name P7 comes from a prefix the attackers used in their programming code. While that detail won't mean much to most iPhone owners, the changes behind it are concerning. The spyware now performs more data collection directly on the infected phone and gives attackers additional control over what happens next. Apple told CyberGuy that DarkSword originated from sophisticated mercenary spyware developed at considerable expense. After the spyware leaked, the technology became available to common criminals.
Once attackers successfully compromise a vulnerable device, P7 DarkSword can reach information that most people would consider deeply private. Researchers identified several capabilities in the spyware's code.
For someone who keeps sensitive documents or financial information on an iPhone, the potential exposure is serious. However, these findings describe the spyware's capabilities. They do not establish that attackers successfully stole every type of information from the device involved in the investigation.
One particularly troubling feature is how frequently the spyware can contact its operators. According to iVerify, P7 DarkSword uses a command-and-control system that can check for instructions every 15 seconds. Attackers can change that interval remotely. This allows the spyware to receive new instructions after the initial infection. For example, an attacker could direct it to collect additional files or examine information stored on the device. The malware also supports commands that scan the phone's file system and execute JavaScript inside its running environment.
Researchers found that the spyware injects its communication component into SpringBoard, a core iPhone system process responsible for the Home Screen and other interface functions. The attackers also removed some diagnostic logging and reduced certain activities that could reveal the infection during an investigation. These changes make the spyware harder for security researchers to examine. However, iVerify did not establish that the malware is completely undetectable.

P7 DarkSword spyware can access sensitive information stored on vulnerable iPhones, including saved credentials, personal photos and Apple Notes. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
DarkSword is associated with an iOS exploit chain that attackers can use to compromise vulnerable devices through malicious web content. Security researchers have linked the P7 variant to distribution through malicious advertisements and compromised websites , sometimes called watering-hole attacks.
That means someone using an outdated, vulnerable iPhone could encounter malicious content while browsing the web, potentially without realizing anything unusual happened. However, these attacks depend on exploitable security weaknesses. Installing Apple's security updates protects against the known vulnerabilities used by earlier DarkSword attacks. The original iVerify investigation focuses primarily on how P7 operates after infection. It does not fully reconstruct how the customer encountered the malicious content. That's why the exact circumstances of that particular infection remain unclear.
Earlier DarkSword attacks targeted iPhones running iOS 18.4 through iOS 18.7. Apple told CyberGuy that it patched the underlying vulnerabilities in 2025, before DarkSword first leaked. The company also released a security update in March 2026 for older devices that could not install newer versions of iOS. According to Apple , iPhones running the latest available updates for iOS 15 through iOS 27 remain protected against the known DarkSword exploits.
Researchers also identified exploit components associated with iOS 18.7 in the newer P7 investigation. However, they have not confirmed that the spyware can compromise fully updated iPhones. As of October 2026, iOS 27 is Apple's current major iPhone software generation. However, the latest available update depends on your iPhone model. Devices that have not received available security updates may remain exposed to known vulnerabilities.
The research is a reminder that even sophisticated phone security can face serious threats. Fortunately, there are steps you can take to reduce your exposure. Start with these protections, especially if you've been putting off a software update.

This setting adds another layer of protection against newly discovered security problems.

France’s bond market hit by another bout of selling as country recovers from weekend protests
Business live – latest updates
French borrowing costs continued to rise on Thursday, as investors fret that France’s government is struggling to pass a federal budget after public protests gripped the country.
France’s bond market was hit with another bout of selling, with the difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs – a metric for the risk premium attached to French debt – rising to its highest level in almost 15 years.
The yield on the French 10-year bond – known as obligation assimilables du Trésor ( Oat ) – rose by nine basis points to 5.089% in early trading on Thursday, its highest level since July 2022. It broke across the 5% threshold on Wednesday for the first time since 2002.
The move lifted France’s 10-year borrowing costs over the equivalent for US Treasury bonds for the first time since 2013.
The volatility comes as the French government struggles to pass a budget for next year, while the country recovers from widespread protests that turned violent last weekend.
Tens of thousands of people had attended peaceful marches to demand more teachers and repairs to decrepit schools, but different groups clashed with police in cities including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille in recent days.
Public buildings were attacked, and thousands of shops and businesses were looted. The interior ministry said there had been nearly 2,400 arrests.
Meanwhile, a parliamentary gridlock has blocked plans by the president, Emmanuel Macron, to increase the state pension age from 62 to 64 and a series of measures designed to rein in state spending.
France’s budget deficit was 5.1% of gross domestic product in 2025, while its debt pile stood at 115.6% of GDP.
It comes as the country also grapples with higher inflation triggered by the war in Iran, with many governments with big debt piles coming under acute pressure.
Jim Reid, a market strategist at Deutsche Bank, said the sell-off in French government bonds was starting to ripple out to other countries, too.

“Among others, the Italian 10-year spread over [German bonds] widened 3.8 basis points to 116 basis points, while Spain’s widened 3.1 basis points to 66 basis points, marking its widest level since June 2025,” he said.
Carsten Brzeski of the bank ING said rising yields had reinforced the European Central Bank’s “restrictive” monetary policy stance before its interest rate decision next week. The bank last raised its key interest rate to 2.5% in September .
“The ECB is very likely to stay on hold next week and will delay any next rate hike decision to December,” he said.
“Any solution to the current French fiscal woes could bring some relief to bond markets and allow the ECB to continue hiking rates. Without any solution, bond markets have taken over the ECB’s role, making rate hikes less likely.”

The world’s richest man has publicly backed a potential combination of SpaceX and Tesla in what could be the biggest merger in history.
On Tuesday, Elon Musk , the CEO and largest shareholder of both companies, said the electric vehicle maker and the rocket company had formed special committees at the request of shareholders to discuss the idea.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, ​and there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating,” Musk told SpaceX investors on a conference call.
“I think it would be a good ​idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,” he added.
The committees, which are made up of independent directors, would need to agree on the transaction terms of any deal before putting it to shareholders for a vote. Musk said his conflict of interest prevents him from participating in their discussions.
Musk has previously teased a Tesla-SpaceX merger. On a July 22 earnings call, Musk said there was “more and more overlap” between Tesla and SpaceX as the companies expand into artificial intelligence and robotics. Last week, Barclays analysts suggested that a merger could be announced before Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting in December.
Tuesday’s call was the first confirmation that the companies were formally exploring a combination.
A merger could create a company worth around $3.5 trillion , putting it among the world’s most valuable companies. It could also become the biggest merger ever by deal value, potentially surpassing SpaceX’s record-setting $250 billion acquisition of Musk-owned AI company xAI in February. SpaceX is currently valued at about $2 trillion, and Tesla at $1.5 trillion. A deal could also help propel Musk back into trillionaire ranks , depending on its terms and how investors value the combined company. Musk owns around 48% of SpaceX and 20% of Tesla.
The shares of both companies rose in after-hours trading on Tuesday. SpaceX, which went public in June, reported a quarterly net profit of $4.4 billion. Musk told investors he expects annual recurring revenue of between $500 billion and $1 trillion by the end of 2027.
Some analysts, however, have warned of regulatory and geopolitical hurdles, particularly in terms of Tesla’s Chinese operations and SpaceX’s U.S. defence work. Morningstar analysts said a merger could raise U.S. national security concerns involving the combined company’s supply chain. JPMorgan analysts also flagged regulatory approval in China as a potential stumbling block.
Any deal could also face congressional scrutiny, which could intensify if Democrats win control of either chamber in the coming midterm elections. Democratic lawmakers have previously questioned Musk over conflicts of interest and raised national security concerns about reported Chinese investments in SpaceX. Democrats have also challenged major acquisitions in the past on consumer protection grounds. In June, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D, Mass.) criticized SpaceX’s IPO, citing Musk’s concentrated voting power and weak investor protections—concerns that could resurface in a Tesla-SpaceX merger.
A merger could bring two of Musk’s biggest businesses under one corporate umbrella, making it easier for the companies to move investments and resources between projects. “This would allow him to run all their operations under one roof without tripping on as many governance issues,” wrote Morningstar analysts Seth Goldstein and Nicolas Owens in June. “For example, Musk could move Tesla software developers or engineers to work on SpaceX AI projects, and vice versa, or have Tesla and SpaceX supply one another without the need for related party transaction disclosures or risking shareholder lawsuits claiming the resources of one firm are being diverted for the benefit of the other.”
Analysts noted that Tesla’s robotaxis could benefit from Starlink connectivity, while its autonomous vehicles and Optimus humanoid robots could more closely integrate SpaceX’s AI technology. SpaceX’s planned orbital data centers, meanwhile, could potentially benefit from access to Tesla’s battery and energy storage products.
A combined company could also mean greater control of several stages of the AI value chain, from chip design and planned manufacturing to computing infrastructure, AI software, and its deployment in vehicles and robots.
The companies already collaborate. In March, they announced Terafab , a joint semiconductor manufacturing project intended to produce chips for Tesla’s vehicles and humanoid robots and SpaceX’s planned AI satellites. SpaceX technologies have also been used in some Tesla products, including the new Roadster prototype , which uses SpaceX-developed thrusters.
David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group, told the BBC that a merger also appears to align with Musk’s long-held ambition of colonizing Mars . Musk previously outlined plans to send Tesla’s Optimus robots to the planet aboard SpaceX’s Starship spacecraft.
A merger could also strengthen Musk’s influence over Tesla’s direction. Barclays estimated that a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla could give Musk around 37% of the combined company while controlling around 56% of its voting power. He currently controls around 82% of voting power at SpaceX and 20% at Tesla . That could represent either a benefit or a risk for shareholders, as decision-making would become faster but have fewer checks.
“One thing I don’t think people talk enough about with SpaceX and Tesla as well: You do still have a huge amount of key-man risk here,” wrote Morningstar analyst David Sekera earlier this month. “God forbid anything were to happen to Elon Musk.”

articles.title_orig: The Nintendo Switch 2 Has Been Hacked, As First Jailbreak Blows The Modding, Emulation, and Homebrew Floodgates Wide Open
articles.title_zh: The Nintendo Switch 2 Has Been Hacked, As First Jailbreak Blows The Modding, Emulation, and Homebrew Floodgates Wide Open
articles.content_orig:
A little over one year after its debut, and a few months after the discovery of a universal exploit , the Nintendo Switch 2 has been hacked, with the first jailbreak option allowing users to mod games and run homebrew software on any current system. However, this isn't a permanent jailbreak, as the exploit requires a specific original Switch game to run every time the system is booted.
This new exploit is a software-only, tethered jailbreak for the Nintendo Switch 2 that allows running arbitrary native code on any system on the latest firmware. This means that users can run homebrew, mod Nintendo Switch 2 games, back up save files, and access most of the Nintendo Switch 2’s peripherals. To demonstrate what can be achieved with this new jailbreak, the exploit developer modded Mario Kart World by adding a few additional characters, such as Peter Griffin and Hatsune Miku .
Given that it usually takes years to find vulnerabilities that allow jailbreaking any gaming system, it won't surprise anyone that the first Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak has been developed using AI tools such as OpenAI Codex . The first step was finding a suitable backward-compatible original Nintendo Switch game, then establishing initial code execution via a 32-bit integer overflow bug in the targeted game's array handling, then manipulating process permissions and hijacking the system loading routines until code execution was reached.
For obvious reasons, we cannot share any more details on this first Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak, but we had the chance to watch the video showcasing modded Mario Kart World and check out the code repository, so we can confirm it is legit. However, since the developer identified the Nintendo Switch game required for the exploit, it will likely take little time for Nintendo to remove it from the eShop and fix the vulnerability.
Still, a Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak opens a world of possibilities for the system. Given how vibrant the modding scene is for many PC games, including emulated titles, having mods for Nintendo Switch 2 games would be amazing. As would be having the possibility to learn more about the NVIDIA DLSS implementation of the system, which has been confirmed to be quite different from the regular upscaler supported by NVIDIA RTX GPUs.
And seeing what some have achieved on modded original Nintendo Switch consoles, including running PC versions of games such as Final Fantasy VII Remake surprisingly well on them, we could be in for a lot of very interesting projects.
About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. 

After joining Wccftech gaming section in 2015, he quickly expanded his video gaming coverage with in-depth reporting, interviews with iconic industry figures such as Grasshopper Manufacture founder and No More Heroes creator Goichi "Suda51" Suda, Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami, Team NINJA's president and Nioh series director Fumihiko Yasuda, and Silent Hill creator Keiichiro Toyama, reviews and on-the-ground coverage of major industry events such as Gamescom and E3.

When he's not reporting or reviewing, Francesco can be found playing the genres he loves most, spending time with his six cats, reading, writing music, playing guitar and drumming for his progressive rock band.

articles.title_zh: Space Debris Found Twice Within Days Amid ‘Growing Casualty Risk’
articles.content_orig:
Indonesia rocket debris? Image credit: BRIN
When it rains space debris.
Two cases of suspected Chinese rocket debris have been reported, in Indonesia and in the United States.
Indonesia’s National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) reports that several bits of debris crashed into an oil palm plantation in Sampit, East Kotawaringin, Central Kalimantan.
BRIN researcher, Thomas Djamaluddin, said the object found on October 19 was a fragment of a Chinese ZhuQue-2E (ZQ-2E) rocket. There is a ZQE code associated with the ZhuQue-2E rocket, he adds.
There is a ZQE code associated with the ZhuQue-2E rocket. Image credit: BRIN
The rocket was developed by LandSpace, a Chinese commercial space startup and departed from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in China on October 14, 2026, carrying ten satellites.
Minnesota object. Image credit: Stevens County Sheriff’s Office
Yet another incident of possible space junk took place on October 14, 2026, at approximately 3:30pm, the Stevens County Sheriff’s Office in Minnesota received a phone call of foreign debris that was found in a cornfield in Scott Township.
“Upon responding, deputies confirmed that a large, metallic object, approximately 11-feet in diameter, presumably a space object, was present in the cornfield,” reports the sheriff’s office.
The Minnesota duty officer was notified of this and federal agencies responded.
“The Sheriff’s Office is working closely with several state and federal agencies to identify and notify the owner of the debris and to plan for removal from the field. Agency officials have determined that there is no danger to the public due to this incident,” the office stated in a press release.
In a twisted bit of irony, the Minnesota debris may also be associated with a LandSpace Zhuque-2E rocket. According to Ars Technica , it could be tied to the rocket’s upper stage, hardware launched from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on September 15.
In both cases – Sampit and Scott Township — the recovered fragments are being examined to help identify their origin.

articles.title_orig: Russia Pounds Kyiv in Overnight Missile and Drone Barrage – 1 Dead, 24 Injured, Including 4 Children
articles.title_zh: Russia Pounds Kyiv in Overnight Missile and Drone Barrage – 1 Dead, 24 Injured, Including 4 Children
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks on Kyiv killed one person and injured 24 others, including 4 children. Strikes damaged metro infrastructure on the South Bridge, an ambulance station, six emergency vehicles, homes and businesses.
Russian forces launched successive waves of ballistic missiles and attack drones against Kyiv overnight into Thursday, Oct. 22, killing one and injuring at least 24 people, including four children, and damaging a metro bridge, an ambulance station, residential buildings and civilian infrastructure across the Ukrainian capital.
Initially, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported in a Telegram update Thursday morning that the number of injured had risen from six to 15, including two 15-year-old children.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
However, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) reported at 7:55 a.m. that one person had been killed and 22 others injured, including four children, in Russian attacks on the capital.
In a statement issued at 9:21 a.m., the Kyiv City Military Administration said that 24 people had been injured, 16 of whom had been hospitalized.
Russian forces launched ballistic missile strikes on six districts of Kyiv starting on the evening of Oct. 21, causing fires and damage, the DSNS said:
Dniprovskyi district: One person was killed, and a child was hospitalized. Homes and vehicles were damaged, while residential and non-residential buildings caught fire. Five other people were injured.
Darnytskyi district: Transport infrastructure was damaged. No injuries were reported.
Sviatoshynskyi district: A non-residential building and a restaurant complex caught fire. The blaze, which covered 1,100 square meters, has been extinguished.
Obolonskyi district: Non-residential buildings were damaged, and fires broke out. Two people were injured. The fires have been extinguished.
Pecherskyi district: Buildings, ambulances and a monastery were damaged. Eight people were injured, including three children.
Holosiivskyi district: Six people were injured when a non-residential building was struck.
The overnight bombardment also damaged metro infrastructure on Kyiv’s  South (Pivdennyi) Bridge, prompting traffic restrictions on a key crossing over the Dnipro River.
In the central Pecherskyi district, Russian strikes damaged an ambulance station and six emergency medical vehicles, according to the mayor.
The latest attack marks another assault on essential civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, with Russian missiles hitting residential neighborhoods, transport facilities and emergency medical services.
The Russian bombardment also struck part of the capital’s metro infrastructure on the South Bridge, a major crossing connecting Kyiv’s two banks.
“As a result of the shelling, part of the metro infrastructure on the South Bridge was damaged,” Klitschko reported on Telegram .
The Kyiv City Military Administration announced traffic restrictions on the bridge in the direction from the right bank to the left bank because of the attack.
The bridge carries both road traffic and a section of Kyiv’s green metro line across the Dnipro.
Damage to the crossing adds pressure to Kyiv’s transport network as the capital faces repeated Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure.
Russian strikes also damaged an emergency medical facility in Kyiv’s Pecherskyi district.
Klitschko confirmed that the damaged building was an ambulance station and that six ambulances had also sustained damage.
No medical personnel were injured, the mayor said.
The damage to emergency medical services came as ambulances and rescue crews were responding to casualties elsewhere in the capital.
The overnight strikes also sparked a fire at a restaurant building in Kyiv’s Sviatoshynskyi district.
The Kyiv City Military Administration reported that the fire broke out following the Russian attack, adding another civilian site to the growing list of damaged properties.
Earlier Wednesday evening, Russian missiles struck residential buildings and businesses in Dniprovskyi district.
Klitschko reported direct hits on a vehicle repair workshop and a private residential building, while debris damaged another house.
Emergency crews were dispatched amid concerns that people could be trapped beneath the rubble.
At another location in the same district, missile debris fell near a gas station, causing additional damage.
In Darnytskyi district, a Russian strike hit the grounds of a transport infrastructure facility, according to the mayor.
Ukraine’s Air Force issued repeated warnings as Russian ballistic missiles approached the capital late Wednesday and after midnight Thursday.
The warnings began during Wednesday evening’s assault, when explosions were reported across Kyiv.
Further ballistic missile threats followed after midnight, including warnings shortly after 12 a.m. and another at approximately 12:31 a.m.
The Air Force also tracked Russian attack drones approaching the Kyiv region and subsequently warned of a drone over the capital.
The successive threats forced residents to remain in shelters as emergency crews responded to damage across multiple districts.
Russian forces launched a massive combined missile and drone attack against Ukraine beginning at 6 p.m. on Oct. 21, targeting Kyiv as the primary strike location, the Ukrainian Air Force reported.
The attack involved Iskander-M and S-400 missiles, Zircon and Oniks missiles, and 210 strike drones, including jet-powered Shahed-type drones, Gerbera and Italmas drones, and Parodiya (Parody) decoy drones.
“The primary target of the strike was Kyiv,” the report said.
The attack was countered by Ukrainian Air Force aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare (EW) and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of Ukraine’s Defense Forces.
As of 9 a.m. on Thursday, preliminary data showed that Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or suppressed 181 Russian drones, including 87 jet-powered Shahed-type drones, Gerbera drones and other types.
“Ten strike drones remain in the air; combat operations are ongoing! Do not ignore air raid alerts!” the Air Force warned at 9.01 a.m.
Russian weapons struck 32 locations, while debris from intercepted drones fell at eight other locations.
The latest strikes came amid renewed US-led diplomatic efforts to negotiate an end to Russia’s war against Ukraine.
On Wednesday, US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg after holding discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and European officials earlier in the week.
The Kremlin subsequently signaled willingness to resume trilateral negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia and the US.
However, Moscow has not abandoned its territorial claims or its opposition to Ukraine joining NATO.
Meanwhile, Russian forces continue attacking Ukrainian cities and essential infrastructure as winter approaches.
Ukrainian officials have repeatedly stressed that any negotiated settlement must include reliable security guarantees to prevent renewed Russian aggression.

articles.title_orig: Serbian Election Underscores the Region’s Long Political Limbo
articles.title_zh: Serbian Election Underscores the Region’s Long Political Limbo
articles.content_orig:
A grassroots student-led coalition threatens to upend Serbia’s political landscape as the EU-candidate country heads to the polls on Sunday
Serbia’s 6.5 million voters go to the polls on 25 October in a watershed parliamentary election characterised by civil unrest, a new political landscape, allegations of irregularities, an uncertain outcome and the potential of far-reaching consequences.
Here is a brief guide to the key issues.
Two events frame this election. The first was the collapse of the Novi Sad railway station canopy in November 2024, which killed 16 people and uncovered massive government and institutional corruption, setting off two years of anti-government protests .
The second was the hero’s funeral accorded to the Serbian general Ratko Mladić, the “Butcher of Bosnia”, who was convicted of orchestrating Europe’s worst massacre since the second world war but buried with military honours in Belgrade last month.
Amid international outrage but intense Serb nationalist pride, the increasingly authoritarian president, Aleksandar Vučić, who has dominated Serbia’s politics for 14 years, resigned to lead his ruling Serbian Progressive party (SNS) list in an attempt to become prime minister .
Against him is the Student List, a grassroots, decentralised, student-led coalition that has evolved from a spontaneous protest movement after the Novi Sad disaster into a serious parliamentary challenger offering a clear alternative to the traditional parties.
It matters because Serbia is an EU-candidate country that continues to balance ties with the west, Russia and China. Media bias, voter intimidation and electoral list irregularities mean any result could be contested, prompting mass protests and exacerbating regional instability.
Vučić’s SNS anchors the “United Serbia” list. The party relies on control of the public purse, favourable media coverage and strong nationalist backing, but its campaign has been overshadowed by accusations of systemic voter manipulation.
The Student List eschews party hierarchies or a single figurehead, preferring locally respected academics and professionals, and operates through university networks. Its quickfire, humorous campaign has mobilised large numbers of disengaged voters.
That means Serbia’s traditional opposition parties have been largely marginalised, with their collective support falling from 30% to 10-15%. Some parties have switched allegiance to the Student List. Others, such as European Serbia, may not clear the 3% electoral threshold.
Meanwhile, Serbia’s rightwing, nationalist bloc is riven with disagreements and has been further weakened by the unexpected withdrawal of the We the Power of the People party over allegations of Russian influence. Some of the nationalist vote may switch to the SNS.
Opinion polls are conflicting and not especially reliable, and there are significant concerns about electoral integrity, with allegations of state violence against opposition activists and government manipulation of voter registration lists and overseas voting arrangements.
Over the past few months some polls have put SNS ahead, some the Student List, and others have forecast a neck-and-neck race. There is therefore a serious risk that whoever claims a 126-seat majority in the 250-strong parliament, the result will be contested.
Analysts at the European Council on Foreign Relations suggest five main possible scenarios . The SNS could score a convincing victory, with the Student List entering parliament as a strong opposition; or a narrower, contested win, leading to street protests and legal challenges.
The result could be inconclusive, with neither main coalition securing a majority. In that case, smaller traditional parties such as the Socialists could become kingmakers, or the election could be re-run.
The Student List could win a majority, but find the result contested by Vučić and the SNS, again leading to protests and possible violent repression; or it could secure a clear mandate allowing a peaceful transfer of power and setting Serbia on a very different course.
Polling stations open on Sunday at 7am local time and close 8pm, with early independent and unofficial projections expected from about 9pm and preliminary official results from the electoral commission in the early hours of the morning.
Within Serbia, the immediate fallout will depend on whether voters accept the result as legitimate. A victory for either side marred by obvious irregularities, or a disputed transition, could lead to civil unrest, violent clashes and institutional paralysis.
Even if the Student List does win and manages a peaceful transfer of power, governing – as Péter Magyar is finding after defeating the illiberall Viktor Orbán in Hungary – will present major hurdles. Reforming 14 years of centralised SNS control will not be easy.
Internationally, the election will affect the EU: an irregular Vučić victory would force Brussels to decide whether to continue transactional diplomacy or freeze integration funds, while a Student win would require immediate financial aid and a clear path to accession.
The Trump administration in the US sees commercial gains in Serbia and launched a “strategic dialogue” with Belgrade in mid-2026 on energy and technology. An SNS-led government would probably maintain Serbia’s awkward geopolitical balancing act.
A Student-led administration, on the other hand, would offer a chance to shift the western Balkan country much more decisively into the European fold.

articles.title_orig: 5 simple ways to relieve the aches and pains of sitting at a desk all day
articles.title_zh: 5 simple ways to relieve the aches and pains of sitting at a desk all day
articles.content_orig:
Back pain, eye strain, sluggishness, shoulder aches, restlessness.
If you sit in front of a computer for long periods of time, whether it's for work or leisure, you've probably experienced one of these symptoms.
But there are ways to relieve some of this discomfort — and even combat some of the health risks that may come with prolonged sitting. That includes walking breaks, ergonomic solutions and quick, simple stretches.
Here's a roundup of tips that have been previously featured on Life Kit.
We know that a sedentary lifestyle isn't great for human health. Studies have shown it can lead to fatigue, weight gain and back and joint pain — and it's been linked to chronic diseases like obesity, heart disease and cancer. Yet adults in the United States spend an average of 9.5 hours sitting per day, involved in activities tied to computers, laptops and phones.
But there may be a way to mitigate its harms. In 2023, researchers at Columbia University Medical Center set out to find the least amount of movement you need to counteract the dangers of prolonged sitting. And they found that walking for five minutes every 30 minutes was the most effective strategy .
In 2023, our colleagues at NPR's Body Electric tested out this five-minute walking exercise on our NPR listeners. Over 20,000 participants joined the challenge — and reported higher productivity and lower fatigue .
Want to give this walking challenge a try? Get instructions from Body Electric — and use this worksheet to keep track of your walking breaks .
Anyone who works at a desk knows how easy it can be to slip into a slouch. If we're not careful, that mid-back rounding can creep into all of our sitting time and create pain by putting stress on the middle section of our spine.
This movement above seeks to relieve that stress and encourage flexibility by mimicking the natural movements of the spine — side bending, bending backward and rotating, says Vinh Pham, a physical therapist. The idea is to get the body comfortable with these motions so that when you encounter them in real life, they're not painful.
To do this modified movement, which Pham calls the 3D T-spine rotation, stand up and drop your right foot behind the left, about a foot apart. Starting with the right arm straight up and the left arm behind you, as if you're shaking the hand of the person behind you, simultaneously drop your arms — still in a straight position — and twist toward your right foot. Move them back to their original position and hold for two seconds. Repeat the movement ten times before switching legs and doing the same exercise on the other side.
For more pain-relieving stretches, read this story.
When you stare at a screen for long periods of time, your eyes have to work hard. They must first turn inward to look at a close subject, then adjust the focus for short vision and hold that position.
Digital eye strain, as eye doctors call it, can cause eye fatigue, headaches or blurry vision. Try the exercise below to relieve that strain.
Fidgeting is a sign you need to break out of a stagnant posture, says Katy Bowman , a biomechanist and author of Rethink Your Position and Movement Matters . Even a position that feels comfortable at first can begin causing back pain, headaches or stiffness if you hold it long enough .
So listen to your body and mix things up. Alternate between sitting, standing, reclining and moving. That might mean opting to stand in the back of a conference room during a big staff meeting, taking a call while going on a walk or reading a report with your feet propped up in the break room.
The goal is to put yourself in configurations that contort your body in different ways. They should be "adaptive and dynamic" and easy to "change in and out of," says Leada Malek , a physical therapist and author of the book Science of Stretch.
Don't worry too much about what is "good" and "bad" posture. Both Malek and Bowman agree on a common phrase among physical therapists: "Your best posture is your next posture."
Your monitor screen should be at eye level so you're not craning your head down to see. And, your keyboard and mouse should be low enough so you're not shrugging your shoulders and lifting up your arms like a praying mantis to type and click.
Meg Honan, a professional ergonomist, says this common "head down and arms up" position sets you up to feel "achy, sore and tired." To combat this uncomfortable and oftentimes painful position, try repositioning your tech. Bring your laptop or desktop monitor screen up to eye level with a stack of books or some other platform.
Place your keyboard and mouse at a lower height where you don't have to shrug your shoulders to use them. If your keyboard is attached to your laptop, consider connecting an external keyboard and mouse so you can have the computer screen at your eye level and lower your arms. External mouses don't just help lower our arms, but they also prevent the constant strain of using a trackpad.
For more ergonomic tips, read our story .
